patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with recurrent kidney stones and urinary infections who joins in 2023. A 14 mm left renal pelvic struvite stone is found in the ED in 2024 and treated by ureteroscopy; in April 2026 she has septic shock from a Klebsiella urinary infection and a venous air embolism when her central line is pulled, and recovers fully.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to establish with the practice. Teaches second grade, said her old office keeps changing doctors on her. History of kidney stones and bladder infections, no daily meds she knows of. Membership details and fee schedule emailed. New patient visit booked for 9/12 at 3:45 (after school). Records release sent to her prior primary care office.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43F here to establish. Left her old practice after a run of new doctors.

Kidney stones: first one in her mid-twenties, several since, all passed at home with fluids and over-the-counter pain medicine. Never needed a procedure, never had one analyzed that she knows of. Dad also forms stones. No flank pain right now.

Urinary infections: a few a year on and off for over a decade, usually handled at urgent care with a short antibiotic. Last one maybe in the spring. Hasn't been told of any resistant bugs. Currently no urinary symptoms.

PMH: as above. PSH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with stones, mother with high blood pressure.
SH: teaches second grade, lives in Florence. Never smoker, does not drink. Single.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well, pleasant. HEENT clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness either side. No edema. Skin unremarkable.

A/P
1. Recurrent kidney stones - none active. Encouraged at least 2.5 L of water daily, she keeps a bottle at her desk but forgets during teaching. Will get her old records.
2. Recurrent UTIs - asymptomatic. Asked her to call us rather than go to urgent care next time so we can culture.
3. Health maintenance - CMP, CBC, lipids, UA today; HIV and hep C screen once. Mammogram ordered. Pap history pending records. Flu and COVID shots next month at a nurse visit.

RTC for yearly physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin, your blood work from Tuesday came back fine: kidney function, calcium, sugar and blood counts are normal; LDL cholesterol is a little above the ideal line, nothing to treat at your risk level; and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. The urine was clean as well. Nice to meet you, and see you at the nurse visit for shots.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office (2016-2023), 41 pages, scanned to media. Summary for PCP:
- Problem list: recurrent nephrolithiasis; recurrent urinary tract infections.
- Medications: none.
- Allergies: none known.
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test 06/2020: negative for intraepithelial lesion, HPV negative.
- Tdap 2017.
- No imaging or stone analysis in the packet.
Health maintenance updated.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after school for flu and COVID shots. No fever today, no prior reactions. Flu vaccine left deltoid, COVID right deltoid. Waited 15 minutes, felt fine, left.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. No prior studies available for comparison. The breasts show scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1, negative. Routine screening in one year.

documents.title: Mammogram result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your mammogram was normal. Next one in a year; we'll remind you.

conditions.label: Calculus of kidney
conditions.note: 14 mm left renal pelvic stone; renal colic

results.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae >100,000 CFU/mL. Susceptible: ciprofloxacin, ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Resistant: ampicillin.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis, renal stone protocol. Left kidney: a 14 mm calculus in the renal pelvis, measured in greatest axial dimension. No hydronephrosis. No ureteral calculus. No perinephric stranding. Right kidney normal in size without calculus or hydronephrosis. Bladder is unremarkable. Liver, spleen, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable on this noncontrast study. Appendix normal. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: 14 mm left renal pelvic calculus without hydronephrosis. No ureteral stone.

reports.text: Single supine view of the abdomen. A radiopaque calculus projects over the left renal shadow, corresponding to the stone seen on same-day CT. No other urinary tract calcification. Nonobstructive bowel gas pattern. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Radiopaque left renal calculus, matching CT; usable for follow-up films.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 04/11/2024.

CC: L flank pain.

HPI: 43 y/o F, hx recurrent kidney stones and recurrent UTIs, here because L flank discomfort has come and gone for a few months, along with feeling run down. Has had a few low-grade temps at home, feels unwell, and notes her urine has been cloudy with a bad smell. No burning with urination, no blood in the urine. UTIs in the past treated at urgent care with short antibiotic courses.

PMH: recurrent nephrolithiasis, recurrent UTI. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father - kidney stones; mother - HTN.
SH: never smoker, no EtOH, schoolteacher.

Exam: afebrile, vitals within normal limits. Uncomfortable but nontoxic. Mild L CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no peritoneal signs. Lungs clear, heart regular.

Data: UA pH 8.5, cloudy, LE 2+, nitrite positive, >50 WBC/hpf, blood negative. Urine culture sent. Creatinine 1.0.
Given how long this has been going on, noncontrast CT A/P obtained along with a KUB: 14 mm stone in the L renal pelvis, no hydronephrosis, nothing in the ureter.

ED course: 1 L NS IV, ketorolac 15 mg IV with good relief.

Impression: L renal calculus with renal colic; alkaline pyuric urine.
Dispo: home. Culture pending - PCP to follow. Follow up with PCP this week and with urology. Return for fever, vomiting, or uncontrolled pain.

documents.title: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - I ended up in the ER last night with my left side. They found a kidney stone, a big one apparently, still in the kidney. They said to see you this week and a urologist. Feeling ok this morning. I can do any day after 3.

documents.title: RE: Was in the ER last night
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, Robin. We have the ER record. You're booked Thursday 4/18 at 3:30. The doctor will also call you once your urine culture is back.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: Culture result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Covering for the weekend. ED urine culture: Klebsiella pneumoniae >100K, sensitive to cipro, ceftriaxone, TMP-SMX; resistant to ampicillin. Called pt - still a dull ache L side, one temp of 99.8 last night, no vomiting. Starting ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x 7 days, sent to her pharmacy. Reviewed tendon and sun precautions. Keep Thursday's appointment; ED if fever climbs or she can't keep fluids down.

orders.reason: 14 mm left renal pelvic stone with Klebsiella UTI

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in the ED 4/11 for L flank pain of a few months' duration. CT there showed a 14 mm L renal pelvic stone, no obstruction. Culture grew Klebsiella, on cipro since Saturday, day 6 of 7. No fevers since Sunday. Urine looks clearer. Flank is down to an occasional twinge. Taking water more seriously.

O: Afebrile, vitals reviewed. Comfortable. Minimal L CVA tenderness, none on R. Abdomen soft.

A/P:
1. L renal calculus, 14 mm, in the pelvis - too large to expect it to pass. Alkaline urine plus a urease-type organism makes an infection stone likely. Urology referral placed; she'd like someone in the valley so she doesn't miss school.
2. Klebsiella UTI - finishing cipro. No test of cure unless symptoms.
3. BMP today to recheck kidney function.
Fluids 2.5-3 L/day.

documents.title: Kidney function
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function and potassium from yesterday are normal. Urology should be calling you within the week; let us know if you don't hear.

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Consult date 05/21/2024.
Reason: L renal stone, referred by PCP.

43-year-old teacher with a long history of stones (all passed spontaneously, none analyzed) and recurrent UTIs. ED visit 4/11 for months of intermittent L flank pain with low-grade fevers; noncontrast CT showed a 14 mm L renal pelvic calculus without hydronephrosis. Urine pH 8.5 with pyuria; culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, treated with ciprofloxacin. Currently asymptomatic.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: father with stones.

Exam: well appearing, no CVA tenderness. Abdomen benign.

Impression: 14 mm L renal pelvic stone. The alkaline urine and urease-producing organism point toward a struvite component; these stones harbor bacteria and should be cleared completely.

Plan: L ureteroscopy with holmium laser lithotripsy and stent, scheduled 6/11 once school is nearly out. Stone will be sent for analysis. Will update PCP.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Operative Report: Left Ureteroscopy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outpatient surgery center, date of surgery 06/11/2024.
Preop/Postop dx: L renal pelvic calculus, 14 mm.
Procedure: cystoscopy, L ureteroscopy with holmium laser lithotripsy and basket extraction, L ureteral stent placement (on a string).
Anesthesia: general.
Findings: normal urethra and bladder. L ureter accepted the scope without dilation. Stone in the renal pelvis, fragmented to dust and small pieces; fragments basketed and sent for analysis. Final pyeloscopy without residual fragment over 1 mm. Stent left with string.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day.
Plan: stent removal in the office in 1 week; renal ultrasound in 6-8 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Stone analysis and urology update
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Faxed from urology: stone analysis from 6/11 procedure - struvite 70%, carbonate apatite 30%. Cover note says stent was pulled in clinic 6/18 without trouble. Scanned to chart, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Your stone analysis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin - urology sent your stone results. It was mostly struvite, the kind that forms around urinary infections, which fits with the cloudy urine and the Klebsiella in April. Glad the stent is out. The best thing you can do is keep the water up and let us culture early if bladder symptoms come back. Urology will see you this summer with an ultrasound.

documents.title: RE: Your stone analysis
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks! Makes sense. First week of summer and I'm already drinking more water than in the whole school year.

reports.text: Both kidneys normal in size, with normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No calculus. No hydronephrosis. Bladder partially distended and unremarkable.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Follow-up 08/06/2024 after L ureteroscopy 6/11. Stent out 6/18. No flank pain, no urinary symptoms since. Stone: struvite 70% / carbonate apatite 30%.
Renal US today: no stones, no hydronephrosis either side.
Impression: stone free.
Plan: hydration; prompt treatment of UTIs with culture; renal ultrasound yearly. Return sooner for flank pain or fever.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Reschedule
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Voicemail from pt: open house at school tomorrow, needs to move her physical. Rebooked 9/24 3:45.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Back at school three weeks; says the water bottle habit has stuck so far.

Interval: L ED visit in April for a 14 mm renal pelvic stone with Klebsiella UTI; treated with cipro, then L ureteroscopy/laser 6/11 at urology. Struvite/carbonate apatite on analysis. Stone free on ultrasound in August. No UTIs since spring.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.
ROS negative.

Exam: well. HEENT normal, neck supple. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Breast exam deferred to imaging per her preference. No edema. Skin normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
- Hx renal stones, stone free - urology yearly US.
- Recurrent UTI - call early for culture.
- Prevention: flu vaccine today. Mammogram ordered. Pap/HPV next due 2025. Colon screening starts at 45, next year. CMP, CBC, UA today.
See her in a year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Robin, everything from your physical is in range, including kidney function and calcium. The urine showed no sign of infection. Have a good fall.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Community pharmacy notification: COVID-19 vaccine (Moderna 2024-25 formula) given 10/08/2024, left arm. Entered in immunization history.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 10/2023. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No new mass, distortion or suspicious calcification. Stable.

documents.title: Bladder infection again?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Since Sunday night I've been running to the bathroom and it burns. No fever, back feels fine. You told me to call instead of going to urgent care so here I am. Can I come in after school?

documents.title: RE: Bladder infection again?
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes - 3:20 today with the doctor. Please don't urinate for an hour before if you can, we'll want a sample. If you get fever, chills or side pain before then, call right away.

documents.title: Acute Visit: Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2 days of frequency and dysuria. No fever, chills, flank pain, nausea. No vaginal symptoms. Not pregnant per pt. Stone free since ureteroscopy last June; last UTI was the Klebsiella in April.

Afebrile. Looks well. No suprapubic or CVA tenderness.
Dip: LE 2+, nitrite +, blood neg. Culture sent.

A/P: uncomplicated cystitis. Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x 5 days. Will check culture against her prior Klebsiella. Fluids. Call for fever or back pain.

reports.text: Both kidneys normal in size and echotexture. No shadowing calculus. No hydronephrosis. Bladder unremarkable.

documents.title: Urology Annual Follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Yearly visit 06/10/2025. One episode of cystitis in February treated by PCP (Klebsiella, nitrofurantoin), no flank pain or fever since. Struvite stone cleared by ureteroscopy 6/2024.
Ultrasound today: no stones, no hydronephrosis.
Plan: continue hydration; repeat ultrasound in one year. Allergies: NKDA.

results.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae in 2 of 2 sets. Susceptible: ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin.
Klebsiella pneumoniae >100,000 CFU/mL. Susceptible: ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis. Comparison 04/2024. Kidneys normal in size bilaterally. No renal or ureteral calculus; the previously seen left renal pelvic stone is no longer present. No hydronephrosis. No perinephric fluid collection. Bladder unremarkable. No free fluid or free air.
reports.conclusion: No urinary tract calculus. No hydronephrosis.

reports.text: Limited bedside study during acute hypoxemia after central line removal. Agitated saline not given. No evidence of intracardiac shunt across the interatrial septum by color flow. Hyperechoic focus within the right ventricular cavity, consistent with air. Left ventricular systolic function normal by visual estimate. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Echogenic material in the right ventricle suggesting air. No intracardiac shunt.

reports.text: Follow-up study. No echogenic material in the right heart chambers. Right ventricular size and systolic function normal. Left ventricular size and systolic function normal. Valves without significant abnormality. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: No residual intracardiac air. Normal biventricular function.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Arrived 04/14/2026 00:20.
45F with prior struvite stone (treated by ureteroscopy 2024) and recurrent Klebsiella UTIs. A day of rigors, fever and L flank pain. Her PCP called ahead.
NKDA. No home meds.
T 39.2, BP 82/48, HR 124. Flushed, ill-appearing. L CVA tenderness.
Lactate 4.2, WBC 19.6, Cr 1.3. Cultures drawn. Noncontrast CT: no stone, no hydronephrosis.
IV crystalloid bolus and IV ceftriaxone. MAP stayed under 65 after fluids; norepinephrine started peripherally and R internal jugular CVC placed under ultrasound.
Impression: septic shock, urinary source. Admitted to the medical ICU.

documents.title: ICU Event Note
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Medical ICU, 04/18/2026 10:20.
Called to bedside. Hospital day 5 for Klebsiella urosepsis with septic shock; off norepinephrine since 4/16, still on ceftriaxone, and the R IJ catheter was being pulled this morning. Within a minute of removal she became short of breath and frightened.
RR 28, SpO2 88% RA, BP 110/70, HR 110. Anxious, speaking in short phrases. Wheezes throughout both lungs.
Bedside TTE: echogenic focus in the RV consistent with air; no intracardiac shunt seen.
Assessment: venous air embolism from CVC removal.
Actions: occlusive dressing on the site, 100% O2 by non-rebreather, turned left side down with the head of the bed lowered. Hemodynamics held without pressors. SpO2 96% on 2 L nasal cannula by noon. Will repeat echo tomorrow; peripheral IV for remaining antibiotics.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 04/14/2026, discharged 04/21/2026.
Principal diagnosis: septic shock from complicated urinary tract infection, Klebsiella pneumoniae (blood and urine), susceptible to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin.
Secondary: venous air embolism at central line removal 4/18, resolved.

Course: Presented hypotensive and febrile with lactate 4.2. Fluids, ceftriaxone, and norepinephrine via R IJ central line for about 48 hours; lactate 1.4 on 4/16. CT showed no stone or obstruction. On 4/18, during line removal, acute dyspnea and hypoxemia (SpO2 88% RA) with diffuse wheezing; bedside echo showed RV air without shunt. Treated with high-flow oxygen and left-side-down positioning; on room air by 4/19, wheezes cleared, repeat echo 4/19 with no residual air and normal function of both ventricles. Switched to oral ciprofloxacin.
Discharge labs: WBC 8.4, Cr 0.9.
Discharge meds: ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID through 4/25 (14 days total).
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within one week; urology as scheduled.

reports.text: Both kidneys normal in size and echogenicity. No calculus. No hydronephrosis. No perinephric collection. Bladder unremarkable.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Visit 06/09/2026. Since last year: admitted in April with Klebsiella urosepsis and septic shock; CT then showed no stone or obstruction. Course complicated by an air embolism at central line removal, fully recovered. Feels well now, no urinary symptoms.
Ultrasound today: no stones, no hydronephrosis.
Impression: stone free, recovered from urosepsis.
Plan: hydration, early cultures through her PCP for any UTI symptoms, ultrasound in one year. Allergies: NKDA.
